## Reviewer status: **approved** (F1 and F2 closed). Claude Opus 5.5, medium effort.

I couldn't edit `/tmp/scan-collision-review/review.json` because I only had read access this session. This is the updated record.

### F1: closed
- **Row limit:** `scan_links.py:21-23` has a fixed `rows = 2`. It tries the source baseline, then one row down, one row up, two rows down, two rows up. Each row tries every lane before moving on. Nothing goes beyond ±2 rows.
- **Text block:** `typography_tex.py:1025-1026` sets top = `\paperheight-1in-\voffset-\topmargin-\headheight-\headsep` and bottom = top − `\textheight`. Both are measured upward from the bottom of the page, the same way `\zposy` is, so the bounds are right. Line 31 enforces both. Links can no longer land in the running head or footer.
- **Error:** when no row or lane fits, it raises `Source-link margin full on physical page N` (lines 46-47). That is the absolute page, which suits books whose page counters restart.
- **Test:** `test_crowded_markers_fail_before_leaving_nearby_text_rows` allows 2 lanes, and with bounds 370–430 four rows fit. The first 8 links are placed, the 9th raises the error, and every placed box stays inside the bounds. The test confirms all of that.
- Minor: in that test the tight bounds stop placement before the two-row limit does, so no test exercises the limit alone. The code is plain enough that this doesn't block.

### F2: closed
- **Box nesting:** lines 1043-1044 now read `\raisebox{..}[0pt][0pt]{\hbox{\OSScanLink{#1}}}`. The link is inside the inner hbox, which keeps its natural size, so the link rectangle takes its height from that box. The raisebox's zero height doesn't affect it.
- **Measured rectangles:** from the output QA JSON, n5 is 10.371 × 9.385pt and n7 is 10.371 × 9.385pt. All four parallel links are the same size.
- **Test:** the real-TeX test asserts width ≥ 8 and height ≥ 8 for English, Hebrew, and Hebrew with line numbers.

### New finding F8: low to medium, not blocking, recommended before merge
**A link on the last line of a full page can move up one line without any error.**
- With `book` and `twoside`, LaTeX fills every page to the bottom (flushbottom). On a full page the last baseline sits exactly at the bottom of the text block.
- The box being checked runs from `y − depth` to `y + height`. If the arrow glyph goes below the baseline at all, the source-line position fails the `>= bottom` check. One row down fails too. One row up succeeds, so the arrow lands beside the second-to-last line.
- I couldn't tell from the artifacts whether the glyph goes below the baseline: the 9.385pt rectangle height is height plus depth plus link padding. None of the sampled links sit on a last line.
- **Fix:** check the baseline against the bounds and let the glyph's depth go below them. Alternatively, subtract `\maxdepth` from the bottom bound. Add a Lua case with `y == bottom` and depth > 0 that expects dy = 0.
- If the arrow does go below the baseline, treat this as must-fix: it is the same misplacement F1 was about, just limited to one line.

### Verified
- **Tests:** `/tmp/scan-link-final-tests.log` shows 237 passed and 159 subtests passed.
  - Small inconsistency: the `"tests"` field in the output QA JSON still says 236 / 158, so that field was written before the last test was added. The PDF checksums and rectangles in it match the rebuilt files you described. I couldn't check file timestamps, so I can't independently confirm that the PDFs were built after the last code change.
- **F6:** `css.py:252` wraps the float rules in `@media (min-width: 40.001rem) { @supports (float: inline-start) { … } }`. Browsers without logical floats keep the base inline link and never get the negative margin. Resolved.

### Accepted exclusions (not blocking, as you stated)
- **F3:** identical arrows are placed nearest the text first, then outward, so the order beside a line can run against the reading direction.
- **F5:** in HTML, several boundaries on a column's final line can add gutter row height. No text width is used, and there is no promise of identical vertical height.
- **F4:** the "margin full" build failure is intentional and the message says what to do. No full-book PDF regression was run: only the 3 day-one settings files use the margin, with the same geometry as the day-two samples. This review does not claim all-book coverage.
- **F7:** coverage is better: there is a real-TeX test with numbered Hebrew, and the 4 real parallel links were checked. The wider matrix is still open: parallel column margins through LuaLaTeX, right binding, restarted page counters, and a check that body text doesn't move.
- Out of scope: the source transcription, which was approved separately.

### Sampled Veahavta presentation: **approved** (these two PDF excerpts only, page 3)
- **Hebrew** (`veahavta-hebrew-fixed-page3.png`): n5 and n7 sit side by side on the first line in the left margin, at x 89.9–100.2 and 77.5–87.9 with a 2pt gap. They don't overlap each other or the text, and both are separately clickable. The text is unchanged.
- **Parallel** (`veahavta-parallel-fixed-page3.png`):
  - Hebrew links (left outer margin): n5 is on verse 5, line 1. n7 is on verse 6, line 2 (עַל־לְבָבֶךָ), which is where the source break is.
  - English links (right outer margin): n6 is on verse 5, line 1, and n8 is on verse 7, line 2.
  - All four links are inside the page and don't overlap, and the column text is unchanged.
- **HTML:** in the browser QA, the wide Hebrew view has 2 non-overlapping links one line apart (25.17px). The wide parallel view has 4 that don't overlap. At 390px the links stay inline with no horizontal overflow.
- I didn't have the paths of the earlier collision screenshots, so I compared against the collision described in the original review rather than side by side with the old images.
- This approval does not cover whole pages, batches, the service, or condition behaviour.
